source_review.notes: Checked the foundational LSM-tree and Bigtable papers, LevelDB implementation notes, current RocksDB leveled, universal, Bloom-filter, and write-stall documentation, and the Monkey, WiscKey, and PebblesDB primary publication records. Current product details are bounded to named implementations and retrieval date; ACM DOI metadata was independently confirmed through Crossref where automated ACM access returned 403.

evidence: Defined user key k, value v, sequence q, snapshot s, memory M, data size N, ratio T, level count L, amplification byte variables, debt B, and Bloom variables m, n, h, and p before formal use.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical sequence, wall-clock time, physical file age, snapshot visibility, and reclamation time remain explicitly distinct.

evidence: Recomputed the 10-bits-per-key optimum h approximately 6.93 and idealized false-positive probability approximately 0.00819.
Recomputed 40 MB/s times six as 240 MB/s, 60 MB/s spare service, and 360,000 MB divided by 60 MB/s as 6,000 seconds or 100 minutes.
Recomputed the capacity example as 1.18 + 0.35 + 0.30 + 0.05 = 1.88 TB.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Decimal storage units and simplifying assumptions are stated; none of these calculations is presented as a universal engine prediction.

evidence: Derived L = ceil(log_T(N/M)) from M T^L >= N under the stated geometric-capacity assumptions.
Checked the classical Bloom approximation p approximately (1 - exp(-hn/m))^h and minimizing h near (m/n) ln 2.
Checked debt stability demand aw, spare service c-aw, and ideal lower-bound drain time B/(c-aw) for c greater than aw.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The formulas are explicitly scoped as simplified accounting or calibration models and exclude picker, skew, cache, compression, and device effects.

evidence: Reviewed crashes around WAL sync, flush, file sync, and manifest publication; corrupt and missing files; full storage; stopped compaction; L0 overlap; hot ranges; large values; long snapshots; TTL; disconnected replicas; stale backups; and repeated restart.
Reviewed present and missing point reads, ordered ranges, filter false positives and unsafe domain mismatch, zero compaction headroom, negative spare service, and temporary-space exhaustion.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The chapter covers correctness, performance, retention, recovery, and distributed-boundary adversarial conditions.

evidence: Checked newest eligible sequence visibility, tombstone precedence, no false-negative component pruning, retained-snapshot equivalence across compaction, WAL-before-retirement, atomic manifest authority, checksum failure handling, and eventual debt drainage.
The finite executable merge checks newest-wins, tombstone non-resurrection, and sorted visible output for the declared fixture.
invariant_checking.notes: The finite model is bounded evidence; WAL, storage, filter, compaction, crash, and distributed invariants received manual premise review.

evidence: Reviewed visibility, compaction-preservation, crash-publication, Bloom one-sided safety, geometric-level-count, debt-stability, and tombstone-safety arguments premise by premise.
proof_review.notes: Each argument identifies assumptions that would invalidate its conclusion, including omitted components, incompatible filters, persistence behavior, retained snapshots, and external stale state.

evidence: Audited separation among logical contract, analytical approximation, invariant, proof obligation, implementation mechanism, current product example, measurement, and finite executable evidence.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No empirical engine-performance result is inferred from the analytical models or Python fixture.

evidence: CPython 3.14.4 reproduced the exact finite sequence/tombstone/range output on Darwin 22.6.0 x86_64.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution establishes only the declared finite in-memory merge behavior in the recorded environment, not storage-engine correctness or performance.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed logical contract, WAL and memtable, immutable tables, point and range lookup, levels, compaction families, visibility, filters, caches, value separation, snapshots, deletion, amplification, and distributed boundaries as distinct concepts.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed sustainable service, write stalls, L0 overlap, temporary/free space, pinned history, tombstone resurrection, full-disk and corruption behavior, publication recovery, bulk ingest, observability, and stateful fault testing.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter derives the storage lifecycle and its invariants from first principles, gives ten distinct worked cases, and progresses five exercises from vocabulary through an unfamiliar replica-and-backup deletion design.

limitations: Internal source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical review only; no external storage-engine maintainer, database vendor, hardware/filesystem expert, security/compliance reviewer, or production operator review is claimed. Conclusions remain conditional on workload, implementation, comparator and filter configuration, durability stack, snapshot and deletion policy, storage hardware, distributed protocol, and finite evidence.
